newsitem.title: MEXICO: Leftist party denounces Mexican murders.
newsitem.headline: Leftist party denounces Mexican murders.

text.p: Four members of a Mexican family were gunned down in southern Oaxaca state on Wednesday in a crime the country's main leftist party said was politically motivated.

Two unknown gunmen wielding an M-1 rifle and a shotgun killed Oliva Vargas Carro, a party activist, her husband, mother and 14-year-old son in the village of Rio Grande, some 250 miles (400 km) south of the state capital Oaxaca.
"The patio was littered with bodies ... Oliva was preparing breakfast when two men came in and fired at close range," her brother, German Vargas Carro, told Reuters.
"Her mother came running to help her when the men fired at her, then killed (husband) Silviano and the son," he said.

Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) officials said Vargas, 32, had received threats from state police and local political bosses warning her to stop political activities. PRD officials said they told state officials about the threats.
"These deaths could have been avoided had the state government heeded our warnings," Saul Vicente Vasquez, head of the left-of-centre PRD in Oaxaca, told reporters.

He accused the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) of waging a "dirty war" in the region ahead of upcoming national elections on July 6, when Mexicans go to the polls in a key mid-term vote.
"They see heavy losses in the federal elections in these areas and are resorting to this as a political strategy," Vasquez said.
State officials were not available for comment on the allegations.
PRD officials said four other activists in the southern part of Oaxaca have been murdered so far this year after receiving anonymous death threats.
